views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Commit to the high-level talks now under way in Washington (opened Oct 10) and pursue a limited, credible agreement rather than adding fresh escalation. Hold the scheduled Oct 15 tariff increase (25%→30% on $250B of Chinese goods) as conditional leverage, and signal willingness to defer it in exchange for concrete progress on purchases and enforcement, but do not unilaterally roll back tariffs or make large new commitments before Beijing offers matching terms.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat is real but not existential for the US. The dispute is already biting the real economy: the 10Y yield has collapsed from 2.55% to 1.59% (an inverted curve / recession signal), the Fed has cut the funds rate from 2.39% to 1.83%, UMich consumer sentiment has fallen from 100 to 95.5 (after an 89.8 August trough), and industrial production is essentially flat — a material GDP drag concentrated in manufacturing, farming and sentiment, consistent with the +0.4 threat reading. This justifies treating the dispute as a genuine cost rather than pure opportunity. However, the US retains clear leverage: China has resumed buying ~3.5M tonnes of US soybeans since early September, granted farm-goods tariff exemptions (Sept 13), and asked Washington to delay an anniversary-linked hike — concessions that signal Beijing wants a deal. That leverage, plus a resilient dollar and stable credit spreads, argues against panic or maximal concession. The action stance is a modest lean toward negotiation because the costs of further escalation are rising (the imminent Oct 15 hike risks derailing talks and inviting retaliation, and the Oct 7 Entity List addition of 28 Chinese firms — Hikvision, Dahua, AI startups — has already inflamed the atmosphere just days before the talks), while China's goodwill purchases suggest a constructive path is open. With talks only just beginning, holding the Oct 15 hike as leverage and negotiating a phased outcome is more effective than either escalating or conceding prematurely.
key_factors: High-level US-China talks resume in Washington on Oct 10, 2019 — the decision date
Scheduled Oct 15 tariff hike on $250B of Chinese goods from 25% to 30% if no progress
Oct 7 Entity List addition: 28 Chinese firms (Hikvision, Dahua, Megvii, SenseTime, iFlytek) over Xinjiang
China goodwill: ~3.5M tonnes of US soybean purchases since early Sept + farm tariff exemptions
US macro strain: 10Y at 1.59%, Fed funds cut to 1.83%, sentiment 100→95.5, IP flat
US leverage intact: strong dollar, stable credit spreads, China signaling it wants a deal

sources_cited.excerpt: Chinese state media reports soybeans, pork, and some other farm goods will be excluded from additional retaliatory tariffs (goodwill signal ahead of talks).
10Y Treasury yield fell from 2.55% (April) to 1.59% (Oct 9) — flat curve/recession signal.
Fed funds effective rate cut from 2.39% to 1.83% (May-Oct).
Consumer sentiment fell from 100 to 95.5, with an 89.8 August trough.
Talks under way in tense atmosphere; $250B tariff hike to 30% scheduled for Oct 15 if no progress; China booked ~3.5M tonnes of soybeans since early Sept.
US blacklists 28 Chinese entities (Hikvision, Dahua, AI startups) over Xinjiang abuses, days before high-level talks.
